newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse catches breath before Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse catches breath before Fed meeting.

text.p: The Brussels bourse caught its breath on Monday, waiting for the result of a two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee starting on Tuesday, but traders said it would then resume its heady climb.
"A pause for breath and then we will go on up," one share trader said. "There is no reason for (Fed Chairman Alan) Greenspan to raise rates."

Traders said news some of its officers had been questioned by court investigators bruised Kredietbank. The cabinet of Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt was also searched in connection to allegations of special tax deals for banks.
Kredietbank ended down 1.9 percent at 11,550 francs on turnover of more than 15,000 shares -- running against the grain of the wider market which showed little inclination to fall.
Union Miniere (ACUMt.BR), on the other hand, moved up 20 francs to 2,400 on the back of the strong dollar, rising zinc prices and a world stock squeeze for the metal.

Car importer and distributor D'Ieteren added 200 francs at 6,900 after at one stage hitting a year high of 7,030 on news it was contemplating listing hire firm Avis Europe, in which it holds 77.1 percent, on the London Stock Exchange.
Electronics firm Barco continued its recent strong run, rising 100 francs to 5,760 after at one stage hitting a high of 5,800 francs.
Utility firm Tractebel likewise moved up 75 francs to 14,825 francs.
Chemical firm Solvay took heart from the strong dollar, climbing 125 francs to 22,275 francs.
The Bel-20 share index .BFX ended 1.97 points, or 0.1 percent, up at 2,053.51, having moved in a narrow 2,055.43/2,047.61 range.
Analyst Geert Vanderbeke at Generale Bank said the index was well supported at 2,030 and 2,010 but faced resistance at 2,060 and 2,077.
He said there were technical signs the market was about to move higher again after the pause.
